f.title: Consider paediatric-specific aspects for risk identification and characterisation in the RMP
f.statement: Particularly important aspects to be considered for paediatric patients for risk identification and characterisation include: age-related shifts in interaction with target organs or tissues; ontogeny of ADME, including disposition in structures such as the blood-brain barrier; potential adverse reactions from different exposure to metabolites; long-term effects on developing reproductive and neurodevelopmental systems; effects on bone and cartilage during growth; and impact on immune system maturation, including transition from passive maternal immunity.

rows.quote: Particularly important aspects to be considered for paediatric patients for the purpose of risk identification and characterisation include: • age-related shifts in the interaction of the medicinal product with its target organs or tissues; • ontogeny of the absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME), including disposition in intra-individual structures (such as the blood-brain barrier), of an active substance; • potential adverse reactions due to different exposure to (different) metabolites as opposed to the adult age; • long-term effect on developing reproductive and neurodevelopmental systems; • effects on bone and cartilage during active growth phase; • impact on maturation of the immune system in the pathogenesis of known adverse reactions and effect of transition from passive maternal immunity to maturing immune systems in infants.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Support with evidence any claim that a paediatric subgroup does not differ from adults

f.title: Record patient age in paediatric ICSRs as accurately as possible
f.statement: Information on the patient's age in ICSRs should be recorded as accurately as possible: completed days for neonates, days or months for infants and toddlers, and completed years or months for children and adolescents.

f.title: Give age at onset or date of birth (plus gestational age), or the paediatric age subset
f.statement: As far as possible, ICSRs should indicate either the age at time of onset of the reaction or the date of birth (and for neonates, pre-term neonates and infants also the gestational age), or the paediatric age subset where the exact age or date of birth cannot be obtained or personal data protection legislation does not permit it to prevent patient identification, in particular for rare conditions.

f.statement: Information on major developmental parameters such as prematurity, pubertal development stage or cognitive and motor developmental milestones should be collected and reported when relevant to the suspected adverse reaction, because maturation varies highly in children and can be clinically more important than age.

f.title: Collect birth history and developmental parameters for neonates when possible
f.statement: Information on birth history as well as major developmental parameters should be collected when possible and where relevant, as rapidly evolving maturation can reveal factors leading to a different pattern of susceptibility in term or pre-term neonates.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: Additionally, information on birth history as well as major developmental parameters should be collected when possible and where relevant. f.title: Include indication, form, strength, dosage, exposure, weight and height in paediatric ICSRs
f.statement: Paediatric ICSRs should include data as complete as possible on: indication or intention of use (including information to establish association with a medication error or off-label use); pharmaceutical form and strength; dosage prescribed and/or administered (single, daily and/or total dose, dosing schedule), duration and circumstances of exposure, method used to determine dosage and treatment compliance; and weight and height/length at the time of the reaction.
f.clause: P.IV.B.2.2. Other information relevant to the paediatric population

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: Paediatric ICSRs should also include data as complete as possible on: • indication or intention of use, including information needed to establish whether the adverse reaction has developed in association with a medication error or off-label use; • pharmaceutical form and strength of the medicinal product; • dosage prescribed and/or administered (including single, daily and/or total dose as well as dosing schedule), duration and circumstances of exposure, method used to determine the dosage and treatment compliance; • weight and height/length at the time of the reaction, as these can vary considerably across an age group and influence the susceptibility to an adverse reaction.

f.title: Follow GVP Module VII PSUR requirements for paediatric medicines
f.statement: The requirements for periodic safety update reports (PSURs) described in GVP Module VII should be followed.

f.title: Monitor the benefit-risk of a paediatric indication via PSURs throughout the life cycle
f.statement: When a paediatric indication has been granted, ongoing monitoring of the risk-benefit balance specifically for that indication should be performed throughout the product life cycle via the PSURs, unless exempted from PSUR submission with a justification.

f.exceptions: Products exempted from PSUR submission with a justification

rows.quote: When a paediatric indication has been granted, ongoing monitoring of the risk-benefit balance specifically for this indication throughout the product life-cycle should be performed (unless exempted from PSUR submission with a justification) via the PSURs, as they are an important tool to collect and cumulatively analyse information on paediatric use.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Address new paediatric safety issues in PSURs overall, by age sub-group and by indication
f.statement: PSURs should explicitly address any new safety issue identified in the paediatric population overall (and, when feasible, by paediatric age sub-group) and by indication; this applies also where paediatric safety information derives from off-label use (including non-age-appropriate formulations or unauthorised sub-groups) or an identified paediatric signal.

rows.quote:
PSURs should explicitly address any new safety issue identified in the paediatric population overall (and when feasible paediatric age sub-groups) and by indication. Discussing and assessing the use of medicines and their effects in real life is the purpose of the PSUR, and this applies not only when a medicine has a paediatric indication but also when information of the safety of a medicinal product used in paediatric patients has been derived from the evaluation of other data related to: • off-label use, including the use of not ‘age-appropriate’ formulations or use in paediatric sub-
groups for which the product is not authorised; or • an identified signal of a paediatric adverse reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Include paediatric exposure by age sub-group and calculation method in the PSUR

f.statement: Where paediatric exposure data are difficult to obtain and validate, estimations based on available sources (GVP Module VII), or a justification if accurate estimation is not possible, should be provided; safety findings from ongoing or completed paediatric clinical trials should also be discussed.

f.title: Higher PSUR frequency may be requested or proposed when a paediatric indication is added
f.statement: Adding a paediatric indication widens the population using the medicine; in certain cases this may lead to a requirement for a higher frequency of PSUR submissions, requested by a competent authority case by case or proposed by the marketing authorisation holder for agreement when the extension of indication is granted.

rows.quote: The addition of a paediatric indication to an existing marketing authorisation implies that the population using the medicine will be widened. f.title: Account for paediatric methodological uncertainties and apply the ENCePP methods guide
f.statement: Lack of consensus on research methods for paediatric aspects (e.g. misclassification of exposure, choice of risk window, imprecise diagnostic coding, medical record limitations) needs to be taken into account to choose the most appropriate approach, and the ENCePP Guide on Methodological Standards in Pharmacoepidemiology should be taken into account.
f.systems: ENCePP Guide on Methodological Standards in Pharmacoepidemiology

rows.quote: There might be a lack of consensus about the best research methodological tools in relation to some aspects characteristic to the paediatric population (e.g. misclassification of exposure data, need to choose appropriate risk window, imprecise diagnostic coding and medical record limitations) and this needs to be taken into account in order to choose the most appropriate approach. The European Network of Centres for Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacovigilance (ENCePP) Guide on Methodological Standards in Pharmacoepidemiology 17 provides useful recommendations to address paediatric-related aspects of observational studies and should be taken into account.

f.statement: Given qualitative differences in medicine usage and adverse reaction reporting, paediatric ICSRs, when they exist, should be analysed independently from ICSRs in adult patients by competent authorities and marketing authorisation holders.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities
rows.quote: Qualitative differences observed in the usage of medicines and in the reporting of adverse reactions have suggested that, when existing, paediatric ICSRs should be analysed independently from ICSRs in adult patients by competent authorities and marketing authorisation holders.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Use tailored statistical approaches for paediatric signal detection by age sub-group
f.statement: When performing paediatric signal detection, tailored statistical approaches and specific tools for a heterogeneous population should be considered, aiming to identify whether in one or all paediatric age sub-groups an adverse reaction is new, more severe or more frequent, or differs in reversibility; with clinical considerations they should also investigate confounding or effect modification by age sub-group.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: When paediatric signal detection is performed, tailored statistical approaches as well as specific tools to study a heterogeneous population should be considered aiming at identifying whether in one or all paediatric age sub-groups an adverse reaction is new, more severe or more frequent than previously known or if there are any differences in the reversibility of the reaction. Together with appropriate clinical considerations, they should also aim at investigating confounding or effect modification by specific age sub-groups.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Adapt statistical signalling thresholds to paediatric exposure
f.statement: When using statistical algorithms in signal detection, the signalling threshold based on the number of ICSRs received should be adapted to the exposure in the paediatric population rather than that of the whole population (exposure calculation per GVP Module VII).

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: When using statistical algorithms in signal detection, the signalling threshold based on the number of ICSRs received should be adapted to the exposure in the paediatric population as opposed to that for the whole population (for exposure calculation, see GVP Module VII).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Underpin paediatric case assessment with a consistent follow-up strategy
f.statement: As the absolute number of paediatric cases is usually small, comprehensive assessment of ICSRs should be underpinned by a follow-up strategy that consistently completes ICSRs with information essential for signal detection and assessment.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: As the absolute number of cases is usually small, comprehensive assessment of ICSRs should be underpinned by a follow-up strategy consistently completing ICSRs with essential information for signal detection and assessment.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Stratify ICSR analysis by age sub-group once enough well-documented cases exist
f.statement: Stratification of ICSR analysis by paediatric age sub-group can be useful to yield additional evidence on age-specific risks, but is scientifically justified only once an adequate number of well-documented cases has been reported.
f.exceptions: Only once an adequate number of well-documented cases has been reported

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote:
Since some adverse reactions might be age-specific, a stratification of the ICSR analysis by age sub-
groups can be useful to yield additional evidence and understanding of the risk and/or risk groups. However, stratification is scientifically justified once an adequate number of cases have been reported and are well documented.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: "can be useful" read as Permitted; actor not named.

f.title: Focus signal detection on paediatric subpopulations by age or maturation status
f.statement: Because the nature and/or severity of paediatric adverse reactions may depend on organ maturation stage, signal detection methods should focus not only on the paediatric population as a whole but also on specific paediatric subpopulations defined by age or maturation status.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: Considering that the nature and/or severity of adverse reactions in paediatric patients may depend on organ maturation stage, any signal detection methods should focus not only on the paediatric 19 Blake KV, Zaccaria C, Domergue F, La Mache E, Saint-Raymond A, Hidalgo-Simon A. Comparison between paediatric and adult suspected adverse drug reactions reported to the European Medicines Agency: implications for pharmacovigilance. Paediatr Drugs. 2014; 16(4): 309-319. Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – P. IV EMA/572054/2016 Page 12/17 population as a whole, but also on specific paediatric subpopulations defined by age or maturation status.
rows.review_note: Review: quote runs across the page break (page furniture kept verbatim). Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Use real-world data or active surveillance where paediatric usage is low
f.statement: For medicinal products with low paediatric usage, a different, more effective approach to signal detection may be needed, for example using real-world data from patient records or disease databases and active surveillance systems.
f.systems: patient records; disease databases; active surveillance systems

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: In case of medicinal products with low usage in the paediatric population, early signal detection can prove more challenging. A different, more effective approach to signal detection may be needed, for example using real-world data from patients’ records or disease databases and active surveillance systems.
rows.review_note: Review: level Recommended ("may be needed"). Double-check: below 90: modal soft; actor not named.

f.title: Follow GVP Modules XV and XVI for paediatric safety communication and RMM
f.statement: For safety communication about paediatric medicines, the general guidance in GVP Module XV (safety communication) and GVP Module XVI (risk minimisation measures) should be followed, together with the additional considerations in P.IV.B.6.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: For safety communication about paediatric medicines, the general guidance in GVP Module XV on safety communication and GVP Module XVI on risk minimisation measures (RMM) should be followed, together with the additional considerations in this Section.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Target paediatric audiences and seek their active participation in communication and RMM
f.statement: Safety communication and communication-based additional RMM should target specific audiences (e.g. paediatricians, parents/carers or legal representatives and the paediatric population, as relevant) and aim to gain their active participation in risk minimisation and informed therapeutic choice, involving the child as appropriate to age; the involvement of children and adolescents in decisions and their information needs should be considered.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: Safety communication and communication-based additional RMM should include targeting specific audiences (e.g. paediatricians, parents/carers or legal representatives and the paediatric population, as relevant) and aim at gaining their active participation in risk minimisation and informed therapeutic choice, involving the child as appropriate to age.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: actor not named; the "should be considered" on involvement of children is from the start of the paragraph.

f.title: Address school, sports, substance interactions, diversion and administration in paediatric materials
f.statement: Marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities are encouraged to address in the product information and any additional RMM such as educational material, as appropriate and if evidence is available: interference with school and sports performance; interactions with alcohol, nicotine and other pharmacologically active substances; risks of diversion of the medicine to friends; and advice on correct administration.

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities
rows.quote: In order to convey information specifically of interest to the paediatric population, marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities are encouraged to address, in the product information and any additional RMM such as educational material, as appropriate, the following if evidence is available and applicable: • interference of the effects of the medicinal product with school and sports performance; • interactions with alcohol, nicotine and other pharmacologically active substances; • risks of diversion of the medicine to friends; • advice on the correct administration of the medicine.
rows.review_note: Review: level Recommended ("are encouraged"). Double-check: quote proves statement and actor.

f.title: Use age-appropriate media and feasible designs for paediatric additional RMM
f.statement: In preparing additional RMM, it is encouraged to consider that children and adolescents may be more effectively reached by tools such as infographics, comics, video clips and age-adapted social media; additional RMM should also be designed with feasibility in mind (integration in the young patient's daily life and acceptability).

rows.quote: Children and adolescents have different media preferences from adults and may be more effectively reached by information and educational tools like infographics, comics, video clips and social media channels adapted to their relevant age group. It is encouraged to consider this in the preparation of additional RMM. Also, additional RMM should be designed with feasibility in mind, e.g. how they can be integrated in the daily life of the young patient and how the acceptability of their use can be optimised.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Test additional RMM messages with the paediatric target group
f.statement: When preparing additional RMM, messages should be tested in conceptual, linguistic and media terms with the paediatric target group, in a way proportionate to the seriousness of the risk.

rows.quote: When preparing additional RMM, messages should be tested in conceptual, linguistic and media terms with the paediatric target group reflecting in a proportionate way the seriousness of the risk.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Help HCPs discuss growth, development and long-term risks with children and carers
f.statement: Safety communication and, when necessary, educational materials addressed to healthcare professionals should aid discussion of certain risks with children and their parents/carers or legal representatives and, where applicable, include advice on common sensitivities and concerns such as effects on growth and development, cognitive and sexual/reproductive functions, and potential long-term effects.

rows.actor: Not specified (marketing authorisation holders and competent authorities)
rows.quote: Safety communication and, when necessary, educational materials addressed to healthcare professionals should aid discussion on certain risks with children and their parents/carers or legal representatives. Where applicable, this should include advice addressing common sensitivities and Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – P. IV EMA/572054/2016 Page 13/17 concerns, such as the impact of the medicinal product on growth and development, cognitive and sexual/reproductive functions, and potential long-term effects.
rows.review_note: Review: quote runs across the page break (page furniture kept verbatim). Double-check: below 90: actor not named.

f.title: Conduct pharmacovigilance as required by Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation 726/2004
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder or applicant in the EU has the legal obligation to conduct pharmacovigilance in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation (EC) No 726/2004.
f.clause: P.IV.C.1.1. Marketing authorisation holder and applicant in the EU

rows.quote: The marketing authorisation holder or applicant in the EU has the legal obligation to conduct pharmacovigilance in accordance with the requirements set up in Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation EC No 726/2004
rows.location: P.IV.C.1.1. Marketing authorisation holder and applicant in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Follow GVP Modules I-XVI with the paediatric considerations of P.IV
f.statement: The marketing authorisation holder or applicant should follow GVP Modules I to XVI, taking into account the paediatric considerations in P.IV, and should follow the guidance in P.IV.A. for addressing paediatric-specific aspects when operating pharmacovigilance processes.
f.clause: P.IV.C.1.1. Marketing authorisation holder and applicant in the EU

rows.quote: and should follow the GVP Modules I to XVI, taking into account the considerations specific to the paediatric population in this P.IV.. The guidance in P.IV.A. should be followed for addressing paediatric-specific aspects when operating pharmacovigilance processes.
rows.location: P.IV.C.1.1. Marketing authorisation holder and applicant in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Carry out PIP studies, including for new indications, forms or routes of SPC-protected products
f.statement: A paediatric investigation plan (PIP) determines the studies that must be carried out in the paediatric population when developing a medicine; this also applies when a marketing authorisation holder wants to add a new indication, pharmaceutical form or route of administration for an authorised medicine covered by a supplementary protection certificate (SPC) or a patent qualifying for an SPC.
f.clause: P.IV.C.2. The paediatric investigation plan in the EU (PIP)

rows.quote: A PIP determines the studies that must be carried out in the paediatric population when developing a medicine. This requirement also applies when a marketing authorisation holder in the EU wants to add a new indication, pharmaceutical form or route of administration for a medicine that is already authorised and covered by a supplementary protection certificate (SPC) or a patent that qualifies for the granting of a SPC (Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006).
rows.location: P.IV.C.2. The paediatric investigation plan in the EU (PIP)
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: development (not PV) obligation restated from the Paediatric Regulation; kept as it conditions PV planning.

f.title: Include results of agreed PIP studies in new marketing authorisation applications
f.statement: All applications for marketing authorisation for new medicines in the EU have to include the results of studies as described in the agreed PIP, unless the medicine is exempt because of a waiver or the results are not yet available due to a deferral.
f.clause: P.IV.C.2. The paediatric investigation plan in the EU (PIP)

rows.quote: All applications for marketing authorisation for new medicines in the EU have to include the results of studies as described in the agreed PIP, unless the medicine is exempt because of a waiver or these are not yet available due to a deferral.
rows.location: P.IV.C.2. The paediatric investigation plan in the EU (PIP)
rows.review_note: Review: no change; legal basis taken from the preceding paragraph. Double-check: below 90: development obligation rather than PV.

f.title: Evaluate PDCO-identified long-term issues for inclusion as RMP risks at initial MAA
f.statement: At the evaluation of an initial (or paediatric line extension) marketing authorisation application, the applicant should evaluate, based on clinical and non-clinical evidence generated after agreement of the PIP, whether issues previously identified by the PDCO (potential long-term safety/efficacy issues for consideration in the RMP) are still valid and whether they should be included as important potential or identified risks in the RMP.
f.clause: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU
f.applicability: Initial or paediatric line-extension marketing authorisation applications with an agreed PIP

rows.quote: At the time of the evaluation of the submission for initial (or paediatric line extension) marketing authorisation, the applicant in the EU should evaluate whether – based on the available clinical and non-clinical evidence generated after the agreement of the PIP - such previously identified issues are still valid, and whether they should be included as important potential or identified risks in the RMP.
rows.location: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Long-term issues linked to off-label use may be treated as missing information in the RMP
f.statement: If no information is available but there is a potential risk related to off-label use, such potential long-term safety issues might also be considered as missing information in the RMP, with the aim of setting up appropriate risk minimisation measures should there be important risks related to paediatric off-label use.
f.clause: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU

rows.quote:
If no information is available, but there is a potential risk related to off-label use, such potential long-
term safety issues might also be considered as missing information in the RMP. The aim would be to set-up appropriate risk minimisation measures, should there be important risks related to off-label used in the paediatric population.
rows.location: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: "might also be considered" read as Permitted.

f.title: Consider key PIP safety-study findings for RMP modules SVII and SVIII
f.statement: If the agreed PIP studies have specific safety objectives (e.g. long-term safety studies) whose results inform existing safety concerns or potential paediatric off-label use, the key findings should be considered for inclusion in RMP part II, modules SVII and SVIII.
f.clause: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU

rows.quote: If there are specific safety objectives in the agreed studies of the PIP (e.g. long-term safety studies), of which results can be informative in consideration of any existing safety concern associated with the medicinal product or with any potential for paediatric off-label use, the key findings of these results should be considered for inclusion in part II, modules SVII and SVIII, of the RMP.
rows.location: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Consider reflecting deferred PIP studies in the RMP
f.statement: If PIP studies are deferred until after initial authorisation in adults, it needs to be considered whether studies included in the PIP should also be reflected in the RMP, taking into account important risks related to potential paediatric off-label use.
f.clause: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU

rows.quote: Furthermore, if a PIP is still to be conducted in paediatric patients following the initial marketing authorisation in adults (i.e. the paediatric clinical studies listed in the PIP opinion are deferred), it needs to be considered whether studies included in the PIP should also be reflected in the RMP taking into account important risks of the medicine related to potential off-label use in paediatrics.
rows.location: P.IV.C.3. The risk management plan in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory ("needs to be considered"). Double-check: below 90: "needs to" read as Mandatory is a judgement call; actor not named.

f.title: Include significant paediatric clinical trial findings in the PSUR
f.statement: Significant findings from ongoing and completed paediatric clinical trials during the PSUR reporting interval should be included in the PSUR, particularly when these trials investigate safety objectives common to the agreed PIP and when the PSUR is due before paediatric development is completed.
f.clause: P.IV.C.4. The periodic update safety report in the EU

rows.quote: Significant findings arising from ongoing and completed paediatric clinical trials during the PSUR reporting interval should be included in the PSUR. This is particularly relevant when these clinical trials investigate safety objectives that are common to the agreed PIP and particularly when the PSUR submission is due before the paediatric development is completed (see P.IV.C.2.).
rows.location: P.IV.C.4. The periodic update safety report in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Higher PSUR frequency via the EURD list may be needed for widened paediatric use
f.statement: When further insight on widened paediatric use is considered beneficial, a higher frequency of PSUR submissions, as required through the List of European Union Reference Dates, might be needed (GVP Module VII).
f.clause: P.IV.C.4. The periodic update safety report in the EU

rows.quote: When it is considered beneficial to gather further insight on widened use of a medicine in the paediatric population, a higher frequency of PSUR submissions as required by means in the List of European Union Reference Dates 21 might be needed (see GVP Module VII).
rows.location: P.IV.C.4. The periodic update safety report in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: level Permitted ("might be needed"); complements the P.IV.B.3 frequency row. Double-check: below 90: modal soft and the frequency is set via the EURD list, not by the MAH.

f.title: Complete the PASS protocol template with paediatric research questions and objectives
f.statement: The PASS protocol template should be completed in accordance with GVP Module VIII and the Guidance for the Format and Content of the Protocol of Non-Interventional PASS, taking into account paediatric specifics; under heading 8 "Research question and objectives", these may relate to alterations in physical growth, puberty, cognitive or physical development.
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.quote:
The template for PASS protocols should be completed in accordance with guidance provided in GVP Module VIII and Guidance for the Format and Content of the Protocol of Non-Interventional Post-
Authorisation Safety Studies 22, taking into account specifics for paediatrics as follows: • template heading 8 “Research question and objectives”: this may relate to alterations in physical growth, puberty, cognitive or physical development;
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Describe linkages to family-member and external data sources in the PASS protocol
f.statement: Under PASS protocol heading 9.4 "Data sources", if information from other family members or external data sources such as census data is needed, the linkages to external data sources should be described (e.g. neonatal exposures and events are often in the mother's record).
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.quote: template heading 9.4 “Data sources”: if information from other family members or from external data sources, such as census data, is needed, the linkages to external data sources should be described (e.g. exposures and events in neonates are often included in the mother’s clinical record rather than in a separate record for the child);
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Adapt PASS statistical methods to paediatric-specific aspects
f.statement: Under PASS protocol heading 9.7 "Data analysis", statistical methods may need to be adapted for paediatric-specific aspects (e.g. correlation of repeated weight and height measurements, changing dosing as the child grows, age-appropriate normalised laboratory values, maturation-related metabolism).
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.quote: template heading 9.7 “Data analysis”: the statistical methods may need to be adapted to account for paediatric-specific aspects (e.g. the correlation between repeated measurements such as weight and height in the same child which may vary in short periods of time, changes in recommended dosing as the child grows, use of age-appropriate normalised laboratory values, metabolism specificities due to maturation).
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: level Recommended ("may need to be adapted" under a "should be completed" lead-in). Double-check: below 90: modal soft.

f.title: Registries may be used for long-term safety of paediatric rare-disease medicines
f.statement: For medicines for rare paediatric diseases with lacking or very limited paediatric data, registries or other means of long-term data collection could be considered by the marketing authorisation holder to enable appropriate PASS to follow up and document long-term safety.
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
f.applicability: Medicines for rare paediatric diseases with lacking or very limited paediatric data

rows.quote: In the case of a development of a medicine to treat rare diseases in paediatric patients for which paediatric data are lacking, or very limited, registries or other means of long-term data collection could be considered by the marketing authorisation holder to enable the conduction of appropriate PASS to follow-up and appropriately document long-term safety.
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Plan paediatric registries and related PASS already at PIP submission
f.statement: In such rare-disease cases, high-level planning of paediatric registries and related PASS should already be considered at the time of submission of a PIP, to promote continuity of safety data generation between pre- and post-authorisation phases.
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.deadline: At the time of submission of a PIP
rows.quote: In these cases, high level planning of paediatric registries and related PASS should already be considered at the time of submission of a PIP (see P.IV.C.2.), to promote continuity in the generation of safety data between the pre- and post-authorisation phase (as already highlighted in P.IV.B.4.).
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.

f.title: Specialist and paediatric trial networks may be consulted on paediatric PASS design
f.statement: Consulting specialist networks (e.g. ENCePP) and, where appropriate, paediatric clinical trial networks (e.g. Enpr-EMA) could be helpful to address specific aspects of the design and conduct of paediatric PASS.
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.quote: The consultation of specialist networks (e.g. the European Network of Centres for Pharmacoepidemiology and Pharmacovigilance (ENCePP) 23) and, where appropriate, the paediatric clinical trial networks (e.g. the European Network of Paediatric Research at the European Medicines Agency (Enpr-EMA) 24) could be helpful to address specific aspects related to design and conduct of
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: split from the scientific-advice row to keep the quote under 1000 characters; quote ends at the page break ("PASS in paediatrics" continues on the next page). Double-check: below 90: quote ends mid-sentence.

f.title: Request EMA scientific advice on complex or innovative paediatric PASS protocols
f.statement: Applicants/marketing authorisation holders in the EU are encouraged to request scientific advice from the Agency on specific aspects of PASS protocols, especially for complex or controversial issues or innovative approaches or methodologies, including those for paediatric studies.
f.clause: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU

rows.quote: The applicants/marketing authorisation holder in the EU is also encouraged to request scientific advice (SA) from the Agency on specific aspects of PASS protocols, especially for complex or controversial issues or for innovative approaches or methodologies including those for paediatric studies 25.
rows.location: P.IV.C.5. Designing a post-authorisation safety study and protocol submission in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: level Recommended ("encouraged"); quote ends with the footnote marker 25 as in the source. Double-check: quote proves statement.

f.title: Analyse paediatric ICSRs separately using EudraVigilance tools such as eRMRs
f.statement: In addition to P.IV.B.5., ICSRs for paediatric patients should be analysed by means of EudraVigilance tools separately from ICSRs for adult patients (e.g. electronic Reaction Monitoring Reports, eRMRs).
f.clause: P.IV.C.6. Signal management within the EU regulatory network

rows.actor: EU regulatory network and marketing authorisation holders (EudraVigilance users)
rows.quote: In addition to the guidance in P.IV.B.5., ICSRs for paediatric patients should be analysed by means of tools provided by EudraVigilance separately from ICSRs for adult patients (e.g. electronic Reaction Monitoring Reports (eRMRs) 26).
rows.location: P.IV.C.6. Signal management within the EU regulatory network
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: section is on the EU regulatory network; MAH applicability inferred from MAH access to eRMRs.

f.title: Calculate SDRs using paediatric ICSRs only to detect paediatric signals
f.statement: It is recommended that statistics of disproportionate reporting (GVP Module IX Addendum I) are calculated using only ICSRs about paediatric patients from appropriate databases (EudraVigilance in the EU); sub-group analysis by age and comparison of paediatric versus adult disproportionality can help determine whether a reaction is more frequent in children.
f.clause: P.IV.C.6. Signal management within the EU regulatory network

rows.actor: EU regulatory network and marketing authorisation holders (EudraVigilance users)
rows.quote:
It is recommended that statistics of disproportionate reporting (see GVP Module IX Addendum I) are calculated using only ICSRs about paediatric patients to increase the ability to detect paediatric signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR) from appropriate databases, i.e. EudraVigilance in the EU. Sub-
group analysis by age and comparison of the disproportionality statistics in paediatric patients versus adults (if applicable, depending on the size of the data set) can help to determine whether or not a suspected adverse reaction is likely to be more frequent in paediatric patients.
rows.location: P.IV.C.6. Signal management within the EU regulatory network
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: actor inferred as for the previous row.

f.title: Children and families may be consulted via young person advisory groups on safety materials
f.statement: Children and their families in the EU can be consulted by the marketing authorisation holder (as well as the Agency and competent authorities) through established young person advisory groups (YPAGs) for the preparation and revision of safety communication and educational materials for additional RMMs.
f.clause: P.IV.C.7. Safety communication in the EU

rows.quote: children and their families in the EU can be consulted by the marketing authorisation holder in the EU as well as by the Agency and competent authorities in Member States through the established young person advisory groups for the preparation and revision of safety communication and educational materials for additional RMMs
rows.location: P.IV.C.7. Safety communication in the EU
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, actor and level.
